subject: HSM gateway attestation & network acceptance for customer-managed VPC
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Customer request: managed HSM in our VPC — network/attestation checklist

Hi Vanessa / team,

We are planning our private deployment with HarborTech HSMs in the Acme Cloud VPC and need a concise list of network boundaries and attestation requirements so our security team can close procurement. High level asks:
- Minimal required inbound/outbound ports and protocols from the HSM gateway to customer services and to Redwood control plane (if any).
- Operator access model & jump host constraints (we prefer no persistent SSH from vendor).
- Evidence we can include in our SOC2 artifact: signed attestation, firmware version proof, and operator activity logs.
- BYOK flow expectations: who wraps keys, where wrapping keys live, and rotation cadence.

Can you provide a one-page acceptance checklist and a network diagram we can hand to our infra team?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Cloud Security — Acme Cloud
priya.shah@acmecloud.com

---
Note: attaching the procurement RFQ separately.
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer request: managed HSM in our VPC — network/attestation checklist

Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching an initial network diagram (acme-hsm-net-diagram-v2.pdf) and a draft handoff checklist (handoff-checklist-v1.xlsx). Key points up front:

- Network boundaries: HSM gateway will live in a private subnet with no internet route. Only specific customer subnets and Redwood-managed monitoring endpoints allowed via explicit SGs/NACLs.
- Ports: KMIP (TCP 5696) inbound from your KMS proxies; TEA/wrap endpoints over mTLS on TCP 443 for wrapping/unwrapping. SSH to the HSM cluster is disabled for vendor operators — operator actions are performed through a guarded jump host with session proxying (details below).
- Attestation: HarborTech provides signed attestation bundles (firmware hash, serial, HSM vendor signature). We will request signed_attestation.pdf and include as part of the SOC2 artifact.
- BYOK: We recommend customer generates a root wrapping key and imports it under an HSM-wrapped envelope. Operational model: HarborTech holds HSM private material; Acme retains the wrapping key material in your KMS under an approved escrow policy.
- Rotation: default rotation of intermediate wrapping keys every 90 days; root wrapping key rotation is on a 12–24 month cadence with documented ceremony.

Next actions: Marcus — can you confirm the minimal egress endpoints Redwood needs for telemetry/heartbeat and whether mutual TLS (mTLS) with client certs is acceptable for our control signals? Soojin — I want the operator access description as a short policy blurb we can include in the procurement attachment. Priya — once we align, I'll generate a DocuSign acceptance page for the HSM attestation.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

- handoff-checklist-v1.xlsx (handoff checklist)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer request: managed HSM in our VPC — network/attestation checklist

Quick technical notes to add to the diagram/checklist:

- Ports/protocols:
  - KMIP: TCP 5696 inbound from Acme KMS proxy to HSM gateway (mutual TLS).
  - Wrap/unwrap APIs: TCP 443 (mTLS) for application-level wrapping; recommend dedicated certs per service.
  - Monitoring/metrics: HTTPS to a Redwood ingress endpoint on a dedicated certificate; IP-restrict this endpoint to our monitoring egress list.
  - NTP only to customer-approved servers over UDP/123 (restrict with NACL).

- Network controls:
  - No NAT gateway on HSM subnets; egress only through a controlled egress proxy in a separate infra subnet for signed telemetry.
  - Host-based firewall on gateway to drop all unexpected flows; security groups with explicit source lists for each service role.

- Operator access:
  - Vendor operators must start ephemeral sessions via the customer-managed jump host. We record session output, require MFA, and only allow sudo via an approved just-in-time role.
  - For emergency access, an audited zeroize workflow (signed approval + 2-person authorization) must be logged and attached to the SOC2 artifact.

- Key lifecycle:
  - Root wrapping key: customer-managed, stored in your KMS.
  - Intermediate keys: generated on HSM after import of root-wrapped material; rotate intermediate keys every 90 days.
  - Key import/export: only wrapped exports allowed; never export cleartext private keys.

I'll update the diagram to show the egress proxy IP list. Priya — are you ok with the 90-day intermediate rotation? If you need more aggressive cadence, we can propose 30 days but it will increase operation complexity.

-Marcus
Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: HarborTech: preliminary attestation package & operator access question

Vanessa / Priya — attaching our preliminary signed attestation (harbortech-signed-attestation.pdf). The bundle contains: firmware hashes, HSM serials, vendor-signed attestation timestamped 2026-08-25, and a short FAQ on the secure import ceremony.

Two quick operator-access clarifications:
1) We can support agentless operation via a vendor-managed gateway if Acme wants minimal vendor footprint, but the vendor operators still need an observability path (we can push to an S3 bucket or to your SIEM via HTTPS).
2) For session proxying: we support certificate-based mTLS to the jump host and can require an operator hardware token for MFA. We do not perform direct SSH into HSM hardware.

If you confirm the egress endpoints and the jump host model, we will produce the final attestation bundle and an HSM firmware-rotation schedule.

Regards,
HarborTech Security Team
security@harbortech.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Operator access policy blurb + audit requirements

Priya / Vanessa — draft blurb you can drop into procurement/security artifact: 

"Operator access to the HSM gateway is strictly controlled: vendor operators may only initiate ephemeral sessions through a customer-managed jump host that enforces MFA and records session activity. Session initiation requires a ticket link to a JIRA case (example: SUP-1984) and approval from two on-call Acme administrators when the action is outside normal maintenance windows. All operator commands and resulting stdout/stderr are captured and stored in a tamper-evident audit store for a minimum of 12 months. Emergency zeroize operations must be authorized by an annotated DocuSign envelope and executed only after a 2-person review."
Other items: we should also specify log retention (12 months), SIEM ingest format (JSON lines with base64 payloads), and required fields: operator id, session id, start/end, approved-ticket, reason.

I'll add this to the handoff-checklist and push an updated worksheet.

-Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Customer request: managed HSM in our VPC — network/attestation checklist (next steps)

Priya — this is good progress. Summary of agreed acceptance criteria for your procurement doc: 

1) Network: HSM gateway in private subnet with SGs allowing only KMIP (5696 TCP) from Acme KMS proxies, mTLS 443 for wrap/unwrap, and restricted egress to Redwood monitoring IPs. No public IPs on the HSM subnets.
2) Attestation: HarborTech provides signed attestation bundle (attached). Final artifact must include firmware hashes and serials and be delivered prior to cutover.
3) Operator access: vendor operators use customer-managed jump host with MFA, JIT roles, 2-person approval for emergency zeroize. Sessions recorded and retained 12 months.
4) Key lifecycle: customer root wrapping key stored in Acme KMS; intermediate keys generated/imported on HSM, intermediate rotation every 90 days; no plaintext export of private keys.

Open items / asks:
- Priya: confirm 90-day intermediate key rotation or request 30-day if you want faster cadence.
- HarborTech: please confirm the final attestation bundle and provide a short CSV manifest of HSM serials and firmware versions.
- Acme infra: accept the attached net diagram and return any NACL tweaks (we can iterate quickly).

I'll prepare a short DocuSign acceptance page and a 30-minute handoff call. Tentative timeslot: Mon 2026-08-30 10:00 AM PT. Please let me know if that works and Priya whether we should route DocuSign to your procurement mailbox.

Thanks all — attaching the current artifacts and the JIRA pointer.

Vanessa Ortiz
